title: Day, Night and the Moon
seo_title: Year 5 Science: Day, Night and the Moon Worksheets (Earth's Rotation, Moon Phases)
standard_text: Describe the movement of the Moon relative to the Earth. Use the idea of the Earth's rotation to explain day and night and the apparent movement of the sun across the sky.
meta_desc: Free Year 5 science worksheets on day and night and the Moon: the Earth's rotation, the Sun's apparent movement, time differences, daylight hours and the phases of the Moon. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: The spinning Earth makes day and night.
key_sub: The Sun only seems to move; the Moon orbits us about once a month.
body_html:
How to think about it

The Earth spins once every 24 hours, giving day and night.

  • The side facing the Sun has day; the side facing away has night. The Sun only appears to move: it rises in the east and sets in the west.
  • The Earth turns 15° each hour, so places to the east see the Sun first and their clocks are ahead.
  • The Moon orbits the Earth in about a month. It reflects sunlight; its phases are the parts of its lit half we can see.
Example

How far does Earth turn in 4 hours?

15° × 4

Answer: 60°

Example

After first quarter comes?

The lit part grows: waxing

Answer: waxing gibbous

Common mistakes

  • Thinking the Sun moves round the Earth each day.
  • Thinking the Moon makes its own light.
  • Thinking the phases are the Earth's shadow.

faq.q: Why do we have day and night?
faq.a: The Earth spins on its axis once about every 24 hours. The half facing the Sun has day, and the half facing away has night.

faq.q: Does the Sun move across the sky?
faq.a: It only appears to. The Earth spins from west to east, so the Sun seems to rise in the east and set in the west.

faq.q: Why does the Moon change shape?
faq.a: It doesn't. As the Moon orbits the Earth we see different amounts of the half that is lit by the Sun, which gives the phases.

items.q: Why does the Sun seem to move across the sky?
c: The Sun orbits the Earth each day.
The Earth is spinning from west to east.
items.e: Day and night happen because the Earth spins; the Sun only seems to move.

items.q: Why do we always see the same side of the Moon?
c: It spins once in the same time it takes to orbit the Earth.
The other side is dark rock.
items.e: The far side is not always dark.

items.e: Half is always lit.
